newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil pension funds go separate ways in CVRD bid.
newsitem.headline: Brazil pension funds go separate ways in CVRD bid.

text.p: In a surprise move, Brazilian pension fund Sistel said on Thursday it would join the Valecom consortium to take part in the privatization auction of state mining giant CVRD.
Sistel was part of a group of seven pension funds negotiating jointly to enter one of two consortia bidding in the April 29 auction of a 40-45-percent voting stake in CVRD.

The whole group was widely expected to join the consortium led by Brazilian steelmaker CSN rather than Valecom which is being led by Brazilian metal, cement and pulp group Votorantim and South Africa's Anglo-American Corp .

"We will be signing an agreement to join the consortium led by Votorantim," a Sistel spokesman said. "We will not be contributing any money to the consortium. We are just entering with our existing stake in CVRD's voting share capital of 0.8 percent."

Sistel is the second pension fund after Valia to leave the group of seven, which was coveted by both consortia participating in the sell-off because of the joint 12.45-percent voting stake in CVRD already held by the pension fund group.

The pension funds' joint stake, even when reduced to 10.05 percent with the departure of Valia and Sistel, will assure the winning consortium a controlling position in CVRD if it has the funds on its side.
Valia decided to team up with the employees of CVRD, who have the right to buy 4.45 percent of CVRD voting shares, to join whichever consortium emerges as the winner after the auction.
Another pension fund, Centrus, which never belonged to the bloc of seven funds, has also signed an agreement with Valecom. Centrus already has a two percent voting stake in CVRD.
Votorantim Chief Executive Antonio Ermirio de Moraes said Brazil's largest pension fund Previ, the leader of the seven funds, was also likely to join Valecom, local news agency Agencia Estado said.
Previ has the largest voting stake in CVRD of all the pension funds with 6.9 percent.
That would leave Fapes, Funcef and Funcesp with a remaining 3.15 percent joint voting stake.
